subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub adopt a public acceptability rule for agent-directed instructions in SKILL.md/README content, and where should that rule live?
rationale: This changes a marketplace trust boundary rather than fixing broken current behavior, and current docs only cover adjacent execution and audit concepts.

options.title: Accept as policy work
options.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the security-review invariant in specs.

options.title: Fold into manifest RFC
options.body: Treat the borderline cases as dependent on the declared-capability policy and decide both boundaries together.

options.title: Keep as internal judgment
options.body: Leave the boundary inside ClawScan/moderator review for now without promising a public author-facing rule.

recommendation.title: Accept as policy work
recommendation.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the security-review invariant in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is CODEOWNERS-listed on the relevant security docs and ClawScan prompt paths and authored the adjacent current policy language.
